id: AT-VD-03 (visible defaults: source labels, an ambiguous options key, a consent key passed by env)
note: 0.1.2 visible defaults (spec Behaviour 1, AT-VD-03): two pluginConfigs keys for this plugin are ambiguous, so every key is at its default and the block warns with both key names; reset refuses such a file (exit 3) and leaves it as it was. A consent key passed as a plugin option (env) is ignored with the existing `settings file only` note and stays at its default; a protective key the same. A flag sets a key with the label `flag` (settings show takes the same --root and --log-dir as status). A foreign CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with a consent key also passed by flag: the safe value, labelled so, with both notes. reset edits the settings.json of the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR folder, and refuses (exit 3, also as a dry run, nothing written, no backup) a settings.json that has a second name (a hard link to ~/.claude/settings.json, which the consent rule reads as the same file): its atomic write would put a new file under one name only.

steps.name: ambiguous: all at default, one warning naming both keys

stdout_has: ^settings values: 0 not at default, 44 at default$
^warning: several plugin option keys in your settings\.json \("$BRAND@m", "$BRAND@n"\): every key is at its default; remove the one no longer used$
^settings reset: refused, several plugin option keys in your settings\.json \("$BRAND@m", "$BRAND@n"\); remove the one no longer used, then run this again$

steps.name: a consent key and a protective key passed by env: ignored with the note, at default

stdout_has: ^settings values: 1 not at default, 43 at default$

steps.name: a foreign CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and a consent key by flag: the safe value, both notes; other keys from that folder's file

stdout_has: ^note: relaunch_auto: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not ~/\.claude, safe value used$

steps.name: a settings.json with a second name (a hard link): reset refuses, as a dry run too, and writes nothing

stdout_has: ^settings reset: refused, your settings\.json has a second name \(a hard link\) and a reset writes a new file under one name only; edit it by hand or in /config$

steps.name: and with --apply: both names keep the text, no backup

stdout_has: ^settings reset: refused, your settings\.json has a second name \(a hard link\)

steps.name: with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set, reset edits that folder's settings.json and leaves ~/.claude/settings.json

stdout_has: ^settings reset: removed cooldown_ms from \S+/cc1/settings\.json \(plugin options under "$BRAND@m"\)$
